expectations.text: Uses the CRA classification tiers: default category, Important Class I, Important Class II, and critical products — and identifies a firewall as an Important product (Class II per Annex III/IV structure)
expectations.evidence: Identifies the firewall as Class I ('Class I includes, among other things, firewalls... not intended for industrial use... it falls into Class I') — contradicting the ground truth that a firewall is Important Class II

expectations.text: Explains the conformity-assessment consequence: default products may self-assess (internal control); Class I needs harmonised standards or third-party assessment; Class II requires third-party (notified body) conformity assessment
expectations.evidence: Class I ('self-assessment... only if... harmonized standards') and Class II ('cannot self-assess at all — third-party assessment via notified body is mandatory') are covered, but never states that default-category products may self-assess (only 'heavier conformity obligations than the default... tier')

expectations.text: Covers Annex I essential requirements at a high level (secure-by-default, vulnerability handling, SBOM, support period)
expectations.evidence: Mentions Annex I risk assessment, SBOM and vulnerability handling, but no secure-by-default and no support-period coverage — Annex I essential requirements are not actually described

expectations.text: Notes CE marking + technical documentation + EU declaration of conformity obligations from the December 11, 2027 application date
expectations.evidence: Technical documentation and the 'December 2027 full-application deadline' appear, but CE marking and the EU Declaration of Conformity are never mentioned

expectations.text: Mentions that no CRA harmonised standards are cited in the OJ yet / standards are in development — so conformity planning should not assume a presumption-of-conformity shortcut today
expectations.evidence: 'harmonized standards... many are still being drafted by CEN/CENELEC'; 'full application of harmonized standards isn't yet demonstrable for most product categories' — no presumption-of-conformity shortcut assumed
